page: Amazon Web Services r5a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System. The instance features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 24 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7571 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 384.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and includes no local storage, relying on external network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show a distinct contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core execution is constrained, evidenced by bottom-tier results in single-core stress-ng, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests. Conversely, multi-threaded operations scale across the 48 vCPUs, achieving an average Geekbench multi-core score of 6887.0 and 14157.03 in stress-ng multi-core tests. Cryptographic performance is a notable strength due to dedicated hardware acceleration, registering a PassMark encryption score of 38963.39 in the top quartile. Large uncached memory bandwidth reaches 80.56 GB/sec for reads and 39.54 GB/sec for writes, while Redis SET throughput handles 29.32 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost perspective, AMD-based instances in the r5a family offer high memory capacity per resource unit, presenting a cost-effective alternative to comparable Intel platforms for memory-dominant footprints. However, modest per-core throughput makes it less suitable for compute-heavy workloads, single-threaded bottlenecks, or large language model inference. The instance is suitable for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and NoSQL database engines, in-memory data processing, and distributed memory-heavy background batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r5a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations. Built on a 2.5 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor using the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores alongside 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. It includes no local disk storage and lacks integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached volumes, while offering a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate average multi-core processing power and strong cryptographic acceleration, balanced against weak single-threaded instruction throughput and poor medium-scale LLM generation speeds. Given its high 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and cost-effective AMD hardware profile, r5a.12xlarge functions effectively for in-memory caches, distributed memory processing frameworks, medium-to-large database engines, and memory-intensive enterprise web services.
